subject: Packaging consolidation and conditional discount — clarify seat vs runtime credits
messages:
From: Molly Jensen <molly@aldentech.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Consolidation ask + packaging question

Kimberly — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Alden is evaluating consolidation of two separate inference feeds (edge analytics + customer support embeddings) into a single Redwood runtime to simplify ops. Before we proceed, procurement needs clarity on how you treat seat (concurrent inference nodes) credits vs runtime token/compute credits when we consolidate SKUs.

Two specific asks: 
1) If we convert 120 seats from our legacy seat-based plan into a single consumption bundle, how are transitional credits applied month-to-month? We need to understand the burn schedule and any caps.
2) For a conditional discount tied to committed average runtime (p99 latency SLA + 6M committed runtime), is that expressed as a bill credit or a fixed unit price reduction? Legal prefers a credit line item if possible.

Attached our RFP excerpt for the packaging section. Can you propose a structured example (numbers) showing both options?

—Molly
Alden Technologies, Procurement
attachments: ALDEN_RFP_excerpt.pdf (pdf)
From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Molly Jensen <molly@aldentech.com>
Cc: connor.obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Aug 2028 13:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Consolidation ask + packaging question

Molly — thanks for the clear asks and the RFP excerpt. Below is a short worked example and our recommended approach; I also attached a spreadsheet model to this thread.

Short answer: we can express the conditional discount in either way, but they have different operational tradeoffs.

Option A — Bill credit (recommended for short-term migration):
- Scenario: Alden consolidates 120 seats into a consumption bundle at go-live.
- Transitional credits: we provide a 6-month monthly credit that steps down 60% / 30% / 10% / 0% / 0% / 0% (applied as a $ credit on invoice).
- Conditional discount (commit met): a $/token credit applied monthly if averaged runtime meets the agreed threshold over the trailing 30 days.
- Pros: preserves list pricing integrity; easy to reconcile in procurement with a single credit line; reversible.
- Cons: credits look like rebates, which may require finance signoff for accruals.

Option B — Price reduction (preferred for long-term contracts):
- Scenario: same consolidation but we reprice the consumption unit for the committed period (e.g., 12 months).
- Transitional credits: we offer a one-time migration credit that reduces the first invoice(s).
- Conditional discount (commit met): reduced $/token rate across invoices when the commit is satisfied.
- Pros: simpler accounting for Alden (lower unit cost on the invoice); cleaner for tax/forecasting.
- Cons: less flexible for mid-contract scope changes.

Operational note: seat-to-runtime conversion uses a 1 seat = baseline throughput assumption; we'll commit the conversion factor in the SOW and include a runtime buffer to cover burst. I included an example table and the credit_model.xlsx with monthly line items.

If this looks right, we can draft redline language for legal. Connor — can you confirm whether finance needs any additional documentation for the credit approach?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
attachments: credit_model.xlsx (xlsx)
From: connor.obrien@redwood.ai <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Aug 2028 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Consolidation ask + packaging question

Kim — quick finance check: either approach is workable but bookkeeping prefers a price-level change for multi-year deals (Option B) to avoid carrying liabilities for credit accruals. For short pilots or a 6M pilot-to-commit path, Option A is easier to operationalize.

Two things we’ll need if Alden wants credits on invoices:
- A clear amortization schedule for the credit (we typically book as contra-revenue over the credit window).
- PO or signed MOU that references the credit schedule to satisfy auditors.

If legal wants credit represented as a line item, we can surface sample language. Marissa — can you prepare a one-pager for procurement that shows both invoice mockups? I’ll support finance commentary.

—Connor
VP, Sales Operations
From: Molly Jensen <molly@aldentech.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@aldentech.com
Date: Mon, 21 Aug 2028 09:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Consolidation ask + packaging question

Thanks — this is helpful. Procurement and finance favor Option B (price reduction) for a 12-month commitment, but legal likes the idea of a short migration credit to cover our one-time integration work.

Two asks before we move to redlines: 
1) Can Redwood provide an example SOW clause that pins the seat->runtime conversion factor and the buffer approach? We want a mechanism for revisiting conversion if usage materially diverges (>20% delta).
2) Can you send a mock invoice illustrating both approaches side-by-side so our finance team can choose which format to accept for AR?

If we can get those by Wednesday, procurement will try to move to a signed MOU and then legal will handle the DocuSign flow.

—Molly

Note on approvals: because the migration credit is front-loaded in Option A, any credit above $75k requires CRO approval — we'll loop Jordan if the credit in the model exceeds that.

Kim, Connor — I also added a recommended break-fix SLA carveout for the first 90 days to reduce migration risk.
